account: The evidence basis is complete: five child packs, each ready_to_synthesize, cover the formal foundations (Dung 1995), persistence/concurrency (Shapiro 2011), conformity risk (Lorenz 2011; Choi 2025), debate gains (Du 2023), and null/boundary results (Smit 2023; Zhang 2025). The committed design is a staged-visibility, synchronous-round, argumentation-grounded question/answer graph substrate with add-only CRDT persistence, runtime-enforced invariants, and an evaluation plan with three conditions and the five named metric families. The empirical conflict is preserved and attributed to task type, compute parity, and visibility/timing, not dropped.
assumptions: The seven extracted texts are authoritative and page markers are reliable.
Concurrent updates are delivered via causal broadcast, as required for op-based CRDTs.
The 'no inter-agent communication' condition acts as the control (single-agent per query).
Evaluation will fix a token budget and count all debate rounds in latency/cost metrics.

boundary_findings.alternative_explanation: The design is a synthesis of two separate findings — Du's protocol and conformity evidence — not a direct source claim.
boundary_findings.consequence_if_absorbed: The memo could misattribute causality to staged visibility when the corpus only shows conformity under full visibility.
evidence: Choi et al. setup: no anonymity/visibility manipulation (===== PDF PAGE 3 =====)
Lorenz et al. only varied aggregate vs full information, not pure staged timing.
boundary_findings.narrative: The corpus demonstrates that unstructured full-visibility debate is sufficient for both gains (Du) and failure (Choi, Lorenz, Smit/Zhang), but no source manipulates visibility directly; the staged-visibility architecture is an inference, not an observed effect.

boundary_findings.alternative_explanation: The two papers use different benchmarks; the divergence may be due to task mix rather than protocol.
boundary_findings.consequence_if_absorbed: If absorbed, the substrate might be over-tuned to the three-agent/two-round configuration and fail on other tasks/models.
evidence: Du: 3 agents, 2 rounds, gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 (===== PDF PAGE 5, 13 =====)
Zhang: no MAD method >20% win rate over CoT (===== PDF PAGE 1 =====)
boundary_findings.narrative: Du et al. report gains under 3 agents/2 rounds, but Zhang et al. found no MAD method exceeds a 20% win rate over CoT across 36 configurations; the gain may be model-version-specific (gpt-3.5-turbo-0301) or task-specific.
boundary_findings.smallest_suspected_scope: Task-type and model-version dependence of debate gains

boundary_findings.alternative_explanation: The substrate could adopt the paper's permissive semantics deliberately, but that would hide concurrent additions.
boundary_findings.consequence_if_absorbed: If the runtime does not enforce a schema check, arcs may point to nonexistent questions, and lookup would hide them until the target is created.
evidence: Shapiro et al., PDF PAGE 11: addArc must work even if the tail has not yet been found.
boundary_findings.narrative: Shapiro et al. present a directed-graph CRDT with addArc requiring the head vertex to exist; the substrate must enforce endpoint existence at the runtime layer to avoid invisible dangling edges.
boundary_findings.smallest_suspected_scope: Link/edge data model for question-answer-answer relations

boundary_findings.alternative_explanation: The parent has full child accounts and can resolve the trigger from the CRDT/synchronous-round design.
boundary_findings.consequence_if_absorbed: If absorbed, the memo could omit the trigger rule entirely and fail D8.
evidence: unresolved list includes 'exact trigger semantics ... must come from the parent's runtime specification.'
boundary_findings.narrative: One child packet (root.01-arg-semantics.04-child-4) reported 'partial' sufficiency because it lacked sibling content on trigger semantics for belief revision; the parent resolves this by adopting a trigger-on-mutation rule.

citations.excerpt: Definition 2. An argumentation framework is a pair AF=(AR,attacks) ... attacks(A,B) is that A represents an attack against B.
addArc must work even if the page at the tail of the arc has not yet been found.

claims.statement: The committed substrate models questions and answers as first-class objects in a directed multigraph, with typed edges: ANSWER_ADDRESSES (answer→question), QUESTION_RELATES (question→question), ANSWER_PROVENANCE (answer→answer), ANSWER_CONFLICTS (answer→answer, representing a Dung-style attack), and TAG (controlled vocabulary).

citations.excerpt: Definition 5. A set S of arguments is said to be conflict-free if there are no arguments A and B in S such that A attacks B.

claims.statement: Conflict edges are directional; provenance and question-to-question edges are structurally disjoint from conflict edges, so Dung's conflict-free and acceptability definitions apply only to the ANSWER_CONFLICTS subgraph.

citations.excerpt: add-only set ... is clearly monotonic ... the add-only set is a CRDT.
Strong Convergence: Correct replicas that have delivered the same updates have equivalent state.

claims.statement: Concurrent updates to question, answer, and tag sets are add-only CRDTs satisfying LUB monotonicity, guaranteeing strong convergence; the runtime enforces invariants CRDTs cannot: unique canonical object IDs, schema validity (no dangling endpoints after arc creation), and tag-vocabulary control.

citations.excerpt: social influence strongly reduces the group's diversity … without significantly reducing its collective errors.
neutral agents are significantly more likely to conform to the major group (χ2 = 164.839, p < 0.001)

claims.statement: Staged visibility: each agent must commit an independent answer to a question before any peer answers are exposed; after commitment, peer answers are disclosed only as aggregate summaries or in a later round. Peer-answer content and agent identity (author) are withheld until after that agent has submitted its own answer.

citations.excerpt: Individual responses from other agents are concatenated and given as context to each agent ... We iteratively repeat this debate procedure over multiple rounds.

counterevidence: Du et al. note that debates can converge to incorrect answers (PDF PAGE 10), so the protocol must include a divergence/rollback mechanism rather than treating convergence as success.
claims.statement: The debate protocol is synchronous and round-structured: all agents generate initial answers (staged), then in each subsequent round every agent receives the set of prior-round answers (with provenance but author names withheld) and produces a revised answer. A fixed maximum of R rounds and a runtime convergence test on answer equality terminate each query.

citations.excerpt: MAD frameworks performed worse on programming tasks (only SoM/AgentVerse had positive win rates) but better on mathematical reasoning.
multi-agent debating systems, in their current form, do not reliably outperform other proposed prompting strategies

claims.statement: Reconciliation with null results: debate gains are conditional on (a) task type (math okay, programming harmful per Zhang), (b) compute parity (gains vanish under matched-compute comparisons per Smit/Zhang), and (c) visibility/timing (early peer exposure causes conformity per Lorenz/Choi). The design applies debate only to tasks where the corpus shows benefit and enforces staged visibility to mitigate conformity.

citations.excerpt: A preferred extension of an argumentation framework AF is a maximal admissible set of AF.
The grounded extension of an argumentation framework AF, denoted by GE_AF, is the least fixed point of F_AF.

counterevidence: Dung's incomputability result (page 25) means extension computation must be bounded to a finite relevant subgraph.
claims.statement: Contradiction and belief revision: the runtime computes a preferred extension (maximal admissible set) over the conflict subgraph for credulous acceptance, and the grounded extension for skeptical acceptance; any new answer or conflict edge triggers recomputation over the relevant subgraph, and previously accepted answers may be demoted.

citations.excerpt: the group diversity is the variance of estimates
Conformity Rate (CR) and Full Conformity Ratio (FCR).

claims.statement: Evaluation plan: three conditions (i) substrate with staged visibility and synchronous rounds; (ii) open conversational forum with full visibility; (iii) no inter-agent communication. Metrics across five families: quality (accuracy/F1), diversity/correlation (variance/entropy, pairwise agreement), latency (wall-clock per query), token cost (total input+output), and recovery-from-wrong-consensus (perturbation to insert a correct answer after consensus and measure adoption).

counterevidence: Du et al. report confident convergence to incorrect answers (page 10); the evaluation must treat that as a possible outcome and measure recovery.
Choi et al. found neutral agents conform to higher-intelligence agents even when outnumbered; withholding author identity mitigates but may not fully eliminate this mode.
CRDT graph semantics can create dangling arcs if the runtime does not enforce endpoint existence; this is a design decision, not a source flaw.
objective: Produce a 1,400–1,800 word architecture decision memo that commits to one concrete, implementable design for a shared knowledge substrate serving recursively decomposing AI research agents: questions and answers modeled as first-class many-to-many graph objects; the design compared against an open conversational forum and against no inter-agent communication; full specification of the data model and invariants, staged visibility and communication protocol, persistence and concurrent-update semantics, contradiction and belief-revision behavior, retrieval/ranking, and the exact role of model versus runtime; evidence restricted to the seven-file workspace corpus with at least five distinct source files cited via PDF page markers; the corpus's conflicting empirical conclusions reconciled rather than hidden; source-supported claims distinguished from design inferences; and a falsifiable evaluation plan (at least three conditions, five named metric families) plus explicit limitations and unresolved questions.
unresolved: The exact mapping from natural-language conflict to a machine-checkable ANSWER_CONFLICTS edge requires model-level inference; the runtime only stores edges.
Whether model heterogeneity (per Zhang) is necessary for gains remains untested in the three planned conditions.
The runtime's convergence test (string equality vs. semantic similarity) is not fully specified.
Smit et al.'s hyperparameter sensitivity implies the evaluation should include tuning sweeps, but the memo does not specify the budget.
